items.definition:
to undo twisted threads; to solve a mystery
The detective worked to unravel the complex plot.

To equip with computers or automate with computers
The company decided to computerize all its records.

To agree or happen at the same time
I concur with your assessment of the situation.

To arrange cloth or clothing loosely or gracefully
She draped the blanket over the sofa.

To twist together or involve in difficulties
The fishing net began to entangle the boat's propeller.

To undergo fermentation; to stir up trouble
Yeast is used to ferment grapes into wine.

To know or expect beforehand
We couldn't foresee the problems that would arise.

to ask questions of (someone) closely, aggressively, or formally
The police interrogated the suspect for hours.

to prepare and organize for active service or use
The community mobilized quickly to help the flood victims.

to pull something quickly or forcibly; to remove feathers
She carefully plucked a single rose from the bush.

to slope or lean in a particular direction; to present information in a biased way
The roof began to slant after the storm.

to interfere with something in order to cause damage or make unauthorized alterations
Someone tried to tamper with the lock.

to attack continuously with bombs, shells, or other missiles; to assail (someone) with questions, criticisms, or information
The reporters continued to bombard the politician with questions.

to adjust (something) precisely for a particular function
You need to calibrate the scales before weighing the ingredients.

to cause something to change direction
The shield was designed to deflect incoming arrows.

to eat quickly and hungrily
The hungry children devoured their dinner.

to tame an animal and keep it as a pet or on a farm
Humans began to domesticate animals thousands of years ago.

to reduce to the smallest possible amount
We need to minimise the risks before starting the new venture.

to make something personal or individual
You can personalise your phone with a custom wallpaper.

to connect again after a period of separation or disconnection
It was great to reconnect with old friends at the reunion.

to move in a twisting or spiraling motion
The cream began to swirl into the coffee as she stirred it.

to cause someone to suffer a lasting shock
The sudden loss of his pet seemed to traumatize the child.

to move in an energetic or busy manner
The market was bustling with activity.

to subtract or take away
You can deduct business expenses from your taxes.

deduce or conclude from evidence
From his silence, I could infer that he was unhappy.

to select a small number of candidates from a larger group
We will shortlist the best applicants by Friday.

to walk with a proud, confident gait
The peacock strutted proudly with its tail feathers fanned out.

to walk or behave in a very confident and arrogant way
He swaggered into the room as if he owned the place.

impose a misleading belief upon (someone); deceive
Don't delude yourself into thinking it will be easy.

(of an organization or group) break up or cause to break up and stop functioning
The band decided to disband after their final tour.

attract or tempt by offering pleasure or advantage
The store used discounts to entice new customers.

make a low, guttural sound
The pig began to grunt loudly.

to act as an official in charge of something
The referee will officiate the football match.

to grow again; to reform or revitalize
Some animals can regenerate lost limbs.

To beat or move about violently
The fish began to thrash wildly on the deck.

To make practical and effective use of
We need to utilise our resources more efficiently.

turn away (one's eyes or thoughts); prevent or ward off (an undesirable occurrence)
She averted her gaze from the disturbing scene.

convert (a text written in code, or a message in a difficult or illegible handwriting) into ordinary language
I tried to decipher the old letter, but the handwriting was terrible.

to search deeply and laboriously
She wanted to delve deeper into the historical records.

to disrespect (someone)
Don't diss your elders.

To throw (an object) with great force
He watched the waves hurl themselves against the rocks.

To provoke or intensify (strong feelings, especially anger or excitement) in someone; to cause inflammation
His harsh words only served to inflame the already tense situation.

prove (a statement or theory) to be wrong or false
She tried to refute the accusations made against her.

enter the owner's land or property without permission
Do not trespass on private property.

to stun or confuse
The bright flash of light seemed to daze him for a moment.

to search widely for food or provisions
Bears often forage for berries in the forest.

make changes in something established by introducing new methods, ideas, or products
Companies must innovate to stay competitive.

point out the resemblance of (someone or something) to someone or something else
She liked to liken her job to being a detective.

to confirm or assert that someone or something is true or accurate
I can vouch for her honesty.

to stir or mix with force
The machine began to churn the butter.

to explode or cause to explode
The bomb was set to detonate at midnight.

raise (something) by means of ropes and pulleys
They used a crane to hoist the beams into place.

breathe out heavily; express annoyance
She let out a huff of exasperation.

develop industries in a country or region
Many developing nations seek to industrialize rapidly.

equip with a motor
They decided to motorize their old bicycle.

catch (someone) doing something wrong; arrest
The police managed to nab the suspect near the station.

make (something) ineffective by applying an opposite force or effect
The antidote was used to neutralize the poison.

grow or spread over (something) so as to cover it completely
The garden was completely overgrown with weeds.

charge too high a price for
Many tourists feel that the souvenirs are overpriced.

To state openly; to claim.
He professed his innocence despite the evidence.

To state again strongly; to confirm.
The company reaffirmed its commitment to environmental protection.

To beat or pulsate with a strong, regular rhythm.
His head began to throb with pain.

to hint at or refer to indirectly
She didn't mention it directly, but she did allude to the problem.

To have an unintended and unwelcome result
His plan to surprise her might backfire if she finds out too soon.
